content.page_title: Management of patients with concomitant HF and AF
content.summary: Management summarized in Figure 14 includes identification/treatment of triggers of atrial fibrillation (AF), management of heart failure (HF), prevention of embolic events, rate control, and rhythm control. The figure is a flowchart for management of AF in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showing decision nodes for haemodynamic instability, rhythm vs rate control, specific interventions (ECV, PV ablation, AVN ablation, beta-blockers, digoxin, amiodarone), follow-up, and symptom-guided escalation.
management_steps: Identification and treatment of possible causes or triggers of AF
figure_highlights: Top-level recommendations: anticoagulation for preventing embolic events (Class I); treatment of trigger(s) (Class I); optimization of heart failure therapies (Class I).
If haemodynamically unstable -> urgent rhythm control (electrical cardioversion, Class I).
If stable: consider rate control (beta-blockers Class IIa OR digoxin/digitoxin Class IIa OR intravenous amiodarone Class IIa) with assessment of symptom improvement.
If symptoms persist or rhythm control chosen: options include pulmonary vein (PV) ablation (Class IIa) OR amiodarone (Class IIb) OR electrical cardioversion (ECV, Class IIb).
If rhythm control fails or unacceptable, AVN ablation with pacemaker may be considered (Rate control, Class IIb).
Follow-up and reassessment of sinus rhythm and symptoms are indicated.

abbreviations.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
